title: Jumpstart SDK Blueprints: Jamstack + FastAPI + Go HTTP + CLI (retries & streaming ergonomics)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a compact set of opinionated, production-minded example blueprints for SDK users: a Next.js (TypeScript) Jamstack demo, a FastAPI (Python) server example, a minimal Go HTTP server, and a cross-platform CLI. Each blueprint should showcase recommended retry strategies, streaming ergonomics (client/server), token-efficient prompt patterns, and small helper utilities (retry wrapper, streaming iterator, graceful shutdown). The goal is a low-friction set of templates that engineers can copy into new projects and that illustrate SDK best practices for production inference on Redwood.
acceptance_criteria: Four examples present in repo: nextjs-app, fastapi-app, go-server, redwood-cli
Each example includes: README with setup, example prompts, local dev instructions, unit/integration tests, and a small stress test harness
Retry helpers implemented and exported for Python/TS/Go with configurable backoff and idempotency guidance
Streaming examples demonstrate resumable parsing, cancellation handling, and token-aware buffering
CI runs for examples (basic lint/test) and PR linked to SDK docs page
Docs include notes on when to use batching vs. streaming and concrete config samples (batch size, timeout, cache TTL)
tasks: Scope templates and create skeleton repo layout (nextjs/fastapi/go/cli)
Implement TypeScript streaming wrapper for fetch-based streaming with backpressure handling
Add Python async generator streaming helper and retry decorator with jittered exponential backoff
Add Go context-aware stream reader and retryable HTTP client wrapper
Write README and migration notes referencing Redwood SDK methods and config options
Add unit tests and a small local load script to demonstrate latency vs cost tradeoffs
Open PR, request PM + DX review, iterate on feedback, and merge
